findings.current: 在这里，德国童话之路能带你穿过古老的城堡、茂密的森林和不同寻常的村庄——就像我们都熟悉、喜爱的那些故事里的一样。

findings.current: in
findings.proposed: in{[in] her red hat}
findings.reason: The entry 'in=prep. 戴着；穿着' has no highlight spec, so it highlights the sentence-initial 'In' of 'In Alsfeld' (meaning 在). The sense 戴着 belongs to the second 'in' in 'the much-loved girl in her red hat'. Learners would link the gloss 戴着 to the wrong word. Keep the gloss and point the highlight at 'in her red hat'.

findings.current: be called
findings.proposed: called
findings.reason: The text has 'a book called Grimm’s Fairy Tales'. There is no 'be', and only 'called' is highlighted, so the headword 'be called' (被叫作) does not match what is shown. Use the single word called (past participle used as a post-modifier). The gloss should become 'adj. 名为……的；叫作……的' (single word, so it needs a POS).

va.why: 发表在……书中 is an odd collocation, because 发表 goes with newspapers and journals. 收进……书里出版 is exactly what 'published them in a book called …' means. 出版 is still in the publish gloss.
The proposal adds 这门艺术 ('art'), which is not in the EN, and it drops 本身, the word that the highlighted 'itself' (gloss pron. 本身) maps to. The current 讲故事本身的核心 is acceptable Chinese and more precise.

The highlight problem is real: it was confirmed that find() lands on the sentence-initial 'In' at (0,2). But this proposal would put an editing instruction into the on-screen gloss text, and the gloss 'prep. 戴着；穿着' is already correct. The highlight is fixed through the headword spec in index 16.
他们一些……的故事 is ungrammatical because 的 is missing. 包括……等 still says the list is partial, so the meaning stays exact ('some of … include'), and 广为人知的 and 包括 still map to the glossed words.

穿过城堡 is an odd collocation. 穿行于……之间 fits all three nouns and keeps 'can take you through'. 与众不同的村庄 is more natural and matches the unusual gloss's second sense. Optionally, the through gloss here could become 'prep. 穿过；穿行于', as in [15].

Verified with ann_lib.find: the bare 'in' matches 'In' of 'In Alsfeld' at (0,2), where in means 在. in{[in] her red hat} matches (104,106), the 'in' that means 戴着. The bracket syntax is the supported one.

The gloss is not wrong. '~be called{called}' is the project's established convention (also in z07), and be called is how 初中 textbooks teach 'a book called X'. A headword-only change would also leave the gloss without a POS, which breaks the single-word gloss format.

vb.why: 发表在……书中 is an off collocation for stories that were collected into a book. 收进……书里出版 is idiomatic, exact, and contains 出版, which matches the gloss publish = 发表；出版.

The proposal adds 这门艺术, which is not in the EN, and it drops 本身. That breaks the link to the gloss itself = pron. 本身, even though the reason says 'itself' is kept. The current line is literal but accurate and understandable, so changing 直接 to 径直 is a matter of taste.

The diagnosis is right (the highlight lands on the sentence-initial 'In'), but this is the wrong field. Applying it would put the parenthetical note into the visible gloss text. The correct fix is the headword spec in index 16, so this would duplicate it.
他们一些广为人知的故事 is missing 的 and reads ungrammatically. 他们广为人知的故事包括……等 is natural, and 包括/等 keeps the 'some of' meaning that the list is incomplete.

穿过古老的城堡 suggests physically passing through castle buildings. 穿行于……之间 fits all three nouns naturally, and 与众不同的村庄 is the more natural collocation (it is also the gloss's second sense). The meaning is unchanged.

Confirmed: with no surf spec, the highlight lands on 'In' of 'In Alsfeld' (sense 在), while the gloss 戴着；穿着 belongs to 'in her red hat'. ann_lib.find supports the bracket syntax, and the pattern '[in] her red hat' matches exactly once.

The text has 'a book called …' with no 'be', so the headword 'be called' does not match what is highlighted. 'called' as an adjective (having a particular name, as in OALD) is the exact sense. However, changing only the headword, as proposed, would leave a single-word entry with no POS (名为；被叫作), which breaks the rule. The whole entry must change together. z07 uses the same ~be called{called} pattern and should be aligned with this.

findings.proposed: 因此，这些项目可能达不到预期，甚至可能对志愿游客和当地社区都造成伤害。

findings.proposed: 关键在于充分了解情况后再做出决定，让世界变得比你刚开始做的时候更好。

va.why: 'may' covers both 'fail to meet' and 'even do harm'. 甚至可能 keeps the hedge exact without losing naturalness. 甚至会 could be read as a certainty.
Same reason as [6]: the summary should not turn 'may do harm' into a near-certain claim. The current text matches the summary substring.

给……带来 is the idiomatic pattern, and it keeps every element (for local communities / volunteers / bring / energy, skills, kindness). Dropping 了 suits the general statement and matches the summary's wording.

'might' (可能) is a 初中 curriculum modal, not a primary-school word, and it carries the hedge of the sentence. Other passages annotate it the same way (z29 might=v. 可能（会）, z05). The entry is correct for this sentence.

vb.why: 'may' covers both 'fail' and 'do harm'. 甚至会 sounds more certain than the source does, and 甚至可能 keeps the hedge with no loss of naturalness.
This keeps the summary consistent with the corrected sentence. The source only says such projects may do harm.
对……来说，志愿者带来了 copies the English structure and leaves 带来 without a recipient, and 了 wrongly makes a general statement sound like one past event. 给当地社区带来 is idiomatic and exact.
'might' (meaning 可能) carries the hedge in this sentence and is a junior-high word, not a primary-school word. It is already glossed this way in other passages (v. 可能（会）), so adding it is consistent.

'may' is a primary-school-level word that is in the project's basic list. It appears 31 times across 19 passages and is never annotated. Adding it only here is optional and inconsistent, not a required fix.
比你开始时更好 at first reads as if it compares the world with 'you', and 开始 has no object. 比你刚开始做的时候更好 makes it clear that the comparison is with the time you started, and the meaning stays the same.

'serious' modifies the noun 'problem', so it is an adjective. The gloss says adv. while giving the adjective meaning 严重的.

vb.why: The current line reverses the meaning: EN 'can only work in fixed places' is translated as 可以在任何地点工作. The proposed line is exact and matches [3] and the summary.
Wrong number. EN says ten hours, not 两个小时.
The negation is lost. 'will not scare … or harm' must be 不会……也不会……; the current line says the opposite.
The current line is heavy translationese (是……的, 擅长于, 在……的情况下, 进行游动). The proposed line is natural and equally precise, and it still covers be good at, moving, very little and energy.

findings.current: 长期以来，人们一直把它们的智力与猴子甚至人类的智力相比。
findings.proposed: 长期以来，人们一直把它们的智力与猴子甚至人类的智力相提并论。
findings.reason: Here 'compared to' means 'likened to': ravens' intelligence is treated as being on a par with that of monkeys and humans, which is why sentence [1] calls them an exception. The neutral '相比' only says a comparison was made. It leaves out that implication, and a learner may expect a result to follow. '相提并论' carries the intended meaning.

findings.current: 人们一直把它们的智力与猴子甚至人类的智力相比
findings.proposed: 人们一直把它们的智力与猴子甚至人类的智力相提并论
findings.reason: Same issue as sentence [2]. 'Compared to' means 'likened to', i.e. their intelligence is considered comparable. The summary should say this too.

findings.current: 大多数渡鸦都选择了那件工具，即使不能立刻得到食物奖励。
findings.proposed: 即使不能立刻得到食物奖励，大多数渡鸦还是选择了那件工具。
findings.reason: The 即使 clause is tacked on after the main clause, which copies English word order (a Europeanised concessive). Natural Chinese puts the concession first and links the clauses with 还是. The meaning and the 即使 that matches the gloss for 'even' both stay.

findings.current: 这表明，它们能记住怎样使用这件工具，还能提前计划，以便过后得到那份美食。
findings.proposed: 这表明，它们能记住怎样使用这件工具，还能提前计划，以便之后得到那份美食。
findings.reason: 以便过后 mixes registers: 以便 is formal and 过后 is colloquial, and 过后 means 'after some event is over', not 'later on' as a time ahead. 之后 is the natural word for 'later' here. Nothing else changes.

findings.current: adv. 后来；过后
findings.proposed: adv. 之后；以后
findings.reason: In this sentence 'later' looks ahead (get the treat later). Chinese 后来 is only used for past narrative ('afterwards, as it turned out'), so it is the wrong sense here. 之后/以后 is the correct sense and matches the corrected ZH line.

findings.current: 后来，它们有机会从几样东西中做出选择，这些东西包括那件工具和一些没用的物品。

findings.reason: In this sentence 'the treat' is the food reward the ravens get. '款待' (being treated to something, 请客) is a different sense that does not fit and could mislead learners.

findings.proposed: 它们的聪明才智不仅仅体现在解决问题上。

"isn't just about" means intelligence does not only show itself in problem solving. 智力……在于解决问题 is an odd collocation (it reads as if intelligence consists of solving problems). 体现在……上 is idiomatic and states the link clearly.

va.why: The text matches the file. Sentence [1] calls ravens an exception, so 'compared to' here means their intelligence is likened to, and put on a level with, that of monkeys and humans. A bare '把……与……相比' is neutral, and with no result clause after it, it reads as unfinished. 相提并论 is precise, natural and a familiar idiom. The gloss '把……与……相比' can stay as the dictionary sense.
The text matches the summary. This keeps the summary consistent with the corrected sentence [2] and has the same precision benefit.

The text matches the file. Every element is kept: most ravens, chose the tool, even (即使), no immediate (立刻) food reward. In Chinese, putting the concession first with 即使……还是…… is clearly more natural than adding the 即使 clause after the main clause.

The text matches the file. 'later' looks ahead from the planning moment. 之后 states this neutrally and fits the formal 以便. 过后 is colloquial and sounds like 'once it is over'. The rest of the line is unchanged and still precise. This also matches the corrected gloss for 'later' (index 5).

The text matches the file. 后来 can only describe something that already happened in a past story ('afterwards'). Here 'get the treat later' refers to a future reward, so 后来 is the wrong sense. 之后；以后 is the correct sense for this sentence.

The text matches the file. '这些东西包括' repeats 东西 and reads as translationese, and 其中包括 is the idiomatic connector. Naming the agent of the passive 'were given a choice' (研究人员让它们) is standard and accurate in an experiment context. 有机会 added a sense of opportunity that the English does not have. 后来, 选择, 几样东西 and 包括 all still map to the glosses.

The text matches the file. 'the treat' here is the food reward. 款待 (entertaining or treating someone as a host) is a different sense and could mislead learners. The proposed '（作为奖励的）美食；好吃的东西' gives the exact sense used in this sentence.

va.amended_proposed: 它们的智力不仅仅体现在解决问题上。
va.why: The text matches the file. '智力……在于解决问题' is an odd collocation, and '体现在……上' is clearly more natural and keeps the meaning. Replacing 智力 with 聪明才智, though, breaks consistency with sentences [2] and [16] and with the intelligence gloss (智力；智慧). So keep 智力 and change only the predicate. The 'be about' gloss could become '体现在；关乎'.

vb.why: Here 'compared to' means 'likened to': their intelligence is treated as on a par with that of monkeys and humans. 相提并论 states this, while 相比 only says a comparison was made. The new line is natural and adds no error. Consider adding 相提并论 to the compare…to gloss so the gloss matches the line.
Keeps the summary consistent with the corrected sentence [2].

A 即使 clause tacked on after the main clause is a Europeanised word order. Putting the concession first and linking with 还是 is natural Chinese. The meaning is unchanged, and the 即使 that matches the gloss for 'even' stays.
之后 is cleaner after 以便 and matches the corrected gloss for 'later' (index 5). The reason overstates the case, because 过后 can mean 以后. Still, the change is harmless and improves consistency.
This is a real gloss error. 后来 is only used for past narrative and cannot appear in a purpose clause about later time ('plan ahead to get the treat later'). 之后；以后 is the correct sense.

'were given a choice' does not mean 有机会, which adds a nuance of opportunity. 这些东西包括 repeats 东西 and reads as translationese, and 其中包括 is idiomatic. Naming the experimenters as the agent of the passive is standard practice. 选择 and 包括 stay recognisable for the glosses.
款待 (hospitality, being treated) is a different sense that does not fit and could mislead learners. Here 'the treat' is the food reward.

va.why: Matches the file. 太过努力地去表现 is a literal rendering of try too hard to perform, and 表现得太用力 is the idiomatic equivalent (it matches the gloss 用力过猛). Dropping 时 loses nothing. Every clause (come along with, in front of the camera, make…appear stiff, far from welcoming) is still there.
Matches the file. This a smile is generic, and Chinese does not mark a generic noun with 一个. 笑容在不同的文化中可能有不同的含义 is precise and natural, and it matches the summary.

Matches the file, but 对姿势、头发和妆容的担忧 is ordinary, easily read Chinese and mirrors the noun The worry exactly. The proposed verb-phrase subject followed by a comma (担心……，可能会加重压力) reads less smoothly, not more. This is a matter of taste, not a fix.

Matches the file. The objection is fair: 在意 alone looks like a dictionary sense of awareness. But the proposed 察觉 ("to notice, detect") is not the sense used here either. awareness of your appearance means being conscious of how you look. Keep 意识 as the meaning and flag 在意 as contextual with （这里指）, the same convention z40 uses for terrible. That also keeps the link to the translation 更加在意.

Matches the file. gather into folds is the verb gather plus into for the result, and dictionaries list no phrasal verb gather into. The headword to teach is gather. Accepted together with #10, so gather stays annotated.

gather is a junior-high word and is not on the basic list. v. 聚拢；聚集 is the sense used here (the skin draws together). I tested it with the project's find(): it highlights gather and leaves nothing uncovered.

before is a basic word, but here it has the less familiar spatial sense (= in front of), which the rule allows to be annotated. Students could misread before the camera as being about time. prep. 在……面前 is correct, and find() matches it cleanly.

Annotating the make + object + bare-infinitive pattern is worthwhile (z26 does the same). As proposed it fails, because without {surf} find() returns None. The suggested highlight make … appear takes 'appear', so the existing appear entry then cannot match (I tested this with the project's find()). Highlighting only make passes. The gloss follows the existing 使某人（做某事） style.

find sb doing is a key structure, and the gloss is right for this sentence. Without {surf} the matcher finds nothing, and a highlight of find … faking takes 'faking' from the existing fake a smile entry. That entry then fails and 'smile' is left uncovered (tested with find()). Highlighting only find works.

should is on the 基础词 list. The Chinese 应该 already carries the same inferential meaning (这应该会管用), so students are not misled and nothing new needs learning. The proposed gloss 应该（会）（表示推测） is also clumsy.

vb.why: “太过努力地去表现” is a word-for-word rendering of try too hard to perform. “表现得太用力” is idiomatic and matches the gloss 用力过猛, and dropping the extra “时” changes no meaning.
Here “a smile” means smiles in general. Chinese does not add a number word for that, so “一个笑容” is translationese, and it also clashes with the summary. The proposed sentence is precise and natural.

The nominalised subject “对……的担忧” is Europeanised. A verb-phrase subject, “担心姿势、头发和妆容”, is plainer and more natural for 14-year-olds. The meaning is the same and it still matches the worry about gloss.

The objection is right: “在意” is a contextual paraphrase and not a meaning of awareness, so students would learn it wrongly. But “察觉” (noticing/detecting) is not the sense used here either, since this is about being conscious of and attentive to one's looks. “意识；关注” matches dictionary senses (knowing; interest in something) and fits the sentence and its 在意 translation.

“gather into” is not a lexicalised phrasal verb. It is gather plus a result phrase with into. Making it a headword would teach a false fixed phrase, and the ZH “聚拢成” already shows the meaning of into.
gather is a junior-high curriculum word and the right headword. In this sentence it is intransitive (come together), so “v. 聚拢；聚集” is the exact sense and maps to 聚拢 in the ZH.

before here means in front of, a spatial sense students who only know the time sense of before (在……之前) can misread. The same sentence pairs with in front of in sentence 11, so it is worth glossing, and the gloss is accurate.

make + object + bare infinitive is a core junior-high pattern and should be glossed. For consistency with z26's headword “make sb do” and this passage's “cause sb to do 使某人（某物）做”, use the standard headword with 某人（某物）. “make sth do” is a non-standard headword. Highlight make … appear.

find sb doing is a key junior-high structure. It is the main clause of the sentence and is currently not glossed, and the gloss is accurate. Note: “faking” is already highlighted under “fake a smile”, so the highlight for this entry should not overlap it (e.g. highlight “find” only).

vb.amended_proposed: should=v. （情态动词，表示推测）应该（会）
vb.why: should is a curriculum word, and here it has the inferential sense (that should work = 应该会管用), not obligation, so a gloss adds value. The proposed gloss has two stacked parentheticals, which is clumsy, so it is merged into one cleaner label.

va.amended_proposed: 这表明，蜜蜂小小的大脑可能具有相当强的能力。
va.why: Matches the file. The problem is real: 大脑相当有能力 is a clumsy collocation. The proposed 蜜蜂小小的大脑能力可能相当强 can be misread as 小小的「大脑能力」 ("small brain-power"). 可能具有相当强的能力 keeps may (可能), quite (相当), capable (有能力) and tiny (小小的) without that ambiguity, and matches the summary wording in #5.

Matches the file. The current line is a clunky literal rendering of be capable of. The new line keeps the rhetorical 谁知道…呢, renders might as 会 and capable of as 本事, and says what the English says in natural Chinese.
The quoted text matches the summary. It fixes the same awkward collocation as sentence 15, and the wording is identical to the amended sentence 15 (#0), so the two stay consistent.

Matches the file. A clause-initial 有可能， copies It could be that. Moving 有可能 into the predicate keeps the hedge, far less (少得多), actual (实际) and than we thought (比我们原以为的), and reads naturally. The gloss it could be that=有可能 still maps.

Matches the file. The long English-style subject 它们拥有的另一种惊人能力 is replaced by 它们还有一种惊人的能力. 还有一种 covers another, and nothing else is added or lost: similar to that of a few mammals, the examples in brackets, and metacognition are all kept.

va.amended_proposed: ~make sth + adj.{made … easier or harder}=使某物变得……
va.why: make + object + adjective is a key junior-high pattern, and the gloss is correct. The entry needs an explicit {surf}: without one, find() looks for the literal text 'make sth + adj.' and fails. With made … easier or harder it matches and overlaps no existing highlight (tested).

might is on the 基础词 list (top 500 words) and is used here in its ordinary sense of 可能. Within z40, may is also left unannotated in sentences 15 and 18. The rule does not require annotating it, and it adds nothing new to learn.

vb.why: In Chinese, “有能力” is normally said of people, so “大脑相当有能力” is translationese. “大脑能力可能相当强” is natural, keeps may as 可能 and quite as 相当, and still matches the capable gloss.

vb.amended_proposed: 谁知道那些小小的头脑可能会有什么样的本事呢？
vb.why: The current “可能有能力做些什么” is clunky translationese, and “本事” is the idiomatic fix. Keeping “可能会” renders might exactly and lines up with the might gloss added in #16. It still reads naturally after 谁知道.

vb.amended_proposed: 蜜蜂小小的大脑能力可能相当强
vb.why: The fix is needed for the same collocation problem as sentence 15. But the proposed wording does not actually match the new sentence 15 (“具有相当强的能力” is also more stilted), so it should use the same phrasing as #0.

Opening the sentence with a standalone “有可能，” copies the It could be that structure. Moving 有可能 into the predicate is natural Chinese, keeps the hedge exactly and still matches the it could be that gloss.
The long attributive subject “它们拥有的另一种惊人能力” is clear translationese. “它们还有一种惊人的能力，……” is idiomatic, with 还有一种 = another, and the content is unchanged.
make + object + adjective is a core junior-high pattern (z34 glosses make sb angry). It explains the sentence's main structure, and the gloss matches the ZH “让测试变得……”.
might is a junior-high curriculum word that is currently not glossed. The proposed gloss matches z05's format exactly, and it fits the amended ZH (可能会) from #1.
